name: Glendo State Park (Red Hills Campground)
note: Red Hills spreads over a series of pine-dotted hills below red rock cliffs, on a peninsula on the west side of Glendo Reservoir just north of Reno Cove. The park recommends four-wheel or all-wheel drive for sites 12-15, reached by a steep, undeveloped track, and calls site 1's steep, narrow access road best for smaller units; RH08 and RH09 have 20-ft parking, too short for a 23-ft rig; sites 18-22 sit down at the high-water line among scattered cottonwoods and can be affected by high water, and as the reservoir draws down later in summer the shore recedes across bare flats. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: reserve.wyoming.gov (US eDirect API wyordr.usedirect.com/wyomingrdr/rdr/, PlaceId 10 'Glendo State Park', FacilityId 340 'Red Hills', facility point 42.50308333,-104.96624444, read 2026-11-20): 21 web-bookable units - 20 'Campsite Non-Electric' RH01-RH10, RH12-RH15, RH17-RH22 (IsRVSite true; Rate 10.00; MaximumStay 14; 'Unit & Parking Size(ft)': RH02 140, RH04 130, RH19 130, RH10 110, RH03/RH05/RH06/RH21/RH22 100, RH01 85, RH14 65, RH07/RH17/RH20 60, RH18 50, RH15 40, RH13 30, RH12 25, RH08/RH09 20; pull-throughs RH02-RH06, RH10, RH14, RH17, RH20; gravel pads on RH02-RH10 and RH20-RH22, natural ground on RH01, RH12-RH19) + Group Site G11 (230 ft gravel pull-through, 3 camping units) -> real drive-in RV campground; 18 sites are long enough for a 23-ft rig (RH08/RH09 at 20 ft are not), 14 of them outside the 4WD spur. Wyoming State Parks' own Red Hills page (wyoparks.wyo.gov/index.php/about-our-campgrounds/1699-red-hills-glendo, read as search-result text 2026-11-20; the site refuses with an F5 challenge) and its copies on The Dyrt and Campflare (read 2026-11-20): 'Red Hills has 22 campsites, spread out over a large, generally wooded area'; 'Sites 2 -5 are large pull through sites'; 'Site one is a back-in with a steep, narrow access road, and as such is ideal for smaller camping units'; 'Sites 6 through 9 are small sites, suitable for small camping units and/or tent camping'; 'Sites 12 through 15 are undeveloped sites, and are accessed through a steep, undeveloped access road; four wheel or all-wheel drive is recommended'. The 4WD wording covers only the 12-15 spur (imagery: a dirt track south from the RH10/G11 loop); RH02-RH07, RH10, G11 and RH17-RH22 are on the main gravel park road and its loops, so the campground stays with a caveat (the developed-campground-keeps-its-gravel-loops rule for Glendo). Imagery 2026-11-20: gravel road and loops, pull-through spurs, a vault-toilet building by RH18. Not in the DB: no WY name match (6360/15731 are Seminoe's North/South Red Hills); nearest entry 13977 Reno Cove 0.93 km (FacilityId 341, a separate facility on the next peninsula south); Soldier Rock (FacilityId 346, lead 23) lies ~1.2 km further south. Public (state): no price gate.
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-20: Esri World Imagery and USGS 3DEP (elevation.nationalmap.gov 3DEPElevation exportImage, F32) fetched in the identical EPSG:3857 square frame at 420 m and 120 m half-widths (0.84 and 0.24 m/px), with every reserve.wyoming.gov unit point (grid MapInfo, FacilityId 340) plotted and the full-pool contour drawn; all images rendered; raster values at the unit points match epqs.nationalmap.gov point queries. Imagery is drawn down (a pale bare apron 20-60 m wide between the full-pool line and the imaged water). Glendo full pool 4635.0 ft = 1413.51 m NAVD88 (glendo_notes.txt); lidar hydro-flattened water 1412.98 m. Unit points (lidar m) and nearest full-pool crossing (min distance; profiles at 5 m steps on 8 bearings): RH18 1415.7, 26 m (30 m SE); RH19 1414.1, 6 m (10 m E/SE/SW); RH20 1413.1 - at the line; RH21 1415.0, 16 m (20 m SE/S); RH22 1415.4, 28 m (30-35 m E/SE/NE); RH17 1418.2, 29 m (35 m N/NE, a 'steep overlook'); RH08 1417.5 and RH09 1418.0 15-20 m but on a bluff ('a steep drop off before the shoreline', park text) and 20-ft sites; RH12-RH15 17-58 m (4WD-recommended spur); RH01-RH07, RH10, G11 67-135 m and 4-26 m above full pool on the upland ('a fair distance from the water's edge, and have no direct water access', park text). Ground check (120 m frame): RH18-RH22 sit on open bare ground with scattered leafless cottonwoods (single trees 10-20 m apart, no continuous stand or underbrush band) running down to the full-pool line; no berm, riprap or road between. Park text (The Dyrt/Campflare copies of the Red Hills page, 2026-11-20): 'These sites provide the campground's closest access to the water'; 'Sites 18 through 22 are larger, and are down much closer to the water's edge, with partial shade. These last four sites are potentially impacted by high water.' -> five clear waterfront sites (RH18-RH22) within ~30 m of full pool over open ground -> lakefront with a caveat naming them (few-clear-sites rule, AWH 2026-11-10); the drawdown apron counts because these pads sit at the full-pool line (13969 Custer Cove precedent). Contrary: the engine tags every Red Hills unit 'Waterfront Setting: None' (other Glendo facilities carry a type-level 'Reservoir'). Not below the dam.

fees.note: Wyoming's statewide schedule: each night's camping fee is the base rate plus that day's day-use fee plus sales & lodging tax, per vehicle. The booking site shows 'Fees range from $23-41 (Per Night, Per 1 Vehicle)' on every unit.

flags: Waterfront lakefront on five sites (RH18-RH22): unit points 0-30 m from the full-pool contour over open ground with scattered single cottonwoods, and the park's own text says they are 'down much closer to the water's edge' and 'potentially impacted by high water'. Contrary: the booking engine tags every Red Hills unit 'Waterfront Setting: None' (other Glendo campgrounds carry 'Reservoir'), and the full-pool water reaches these sites only around late spring - early summer. Lakeview is the fallback if the reviewer weighs the engine tag or the leafless cottonwoods (partial shade in leaf) as a buffer; the trees are spaced singles, not the continuous stand of 15741 Mule Hill / 15740 Indian Point.

Access: the park recommends four-wheel or all-wheel drive only for sites 12-15 ('accessed through a steep, undeveloped access road'), a spur south of the RH10/G11 loop; kept with the caveat in the note. Site 1 has 'a steep, narrow access road ... ideal for smaller camping units' (85-ft natural-ground back-in). The Dyrt's own intro (not park text) says 'Access is rough, so plan accordingly'; a 2022-08-30 Dyrt review mentions nothing about the road. The Dyrt's feature tag 'Access: Walk-In' contradicts the engine's drive-in pads and pull-throughs and the park text - read as a Dyrt data error.
Rig fit: RH08 and RH09 are 20-ft sites, RH12 25 ft and RH13 30 ft (both on the 4WD spur); 14 sites outside the 4WD spur (RH01-RH07, RH10, RH17-RH22) fit a 23-ft rig, plus group G11.

Pin moved from the engine facility point (42.50308,-104.96624, at RH04 by the main road) to the centroid of all 21 unit points, ~250 m SE; the campground spreads ~650 m (RH01 at the north end, RH21/RH22 at the southeast tip). elevation_meters is Open-Meteo's 1423 m at the pin; lidar puts the units at 1413.1-1439.3 m.
Site counts: the park counts 22 sites; the engine lists 20 individual units + group G11 (no RH16).
Toilets: one vault toilet per the Red Hills page, three on the park's Glendo amenities list, two in The Dyrt's intro - count left out.
